audit.why: Chart reads Skill x5, Locke at first item, Skill late on both layers and matches the packet chart exactly, over a solid 577-game sample at 56.15%. Full and content agree row for row.
audit.corrected: No chart change. Stage reasons corrected where they rested on the false range claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown field named no numbers at all — 'ten seconds of nothing' was the only figure, and Soul Nails, Soul Ignition and Purgatory had none.
audit.why: Soul Nails is 10s at rank 1 down to 6s, Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s, Soul Ignition is 18s at rank 1 and Purgatory is 120s at rank 1 — those are the four windows the lane is played on.
audit.corrected: All four written into breakdown.cooldowns; the Q cadence added to tldr, phases[0].why and breakdown.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields call Locke 'a 125-range champ' and build the whole plan on out-ranging him. His Soul Nails reach 950 against Ziggs' 850 Q — he out-ranges Ziggs. Ashen Pursuit's auto-attack reset is also unnamed as the tell.
audit.why: A Ziggs player told to 'win the lane at range' will sit at 850 believing he is safe and eat nails for free; the real edge is Ziggs' 6s Q cadence against a 10s Q and a 10s blink.
audit.corrected: Reframed tldr, report[0], phases[0].why, breakdown.early and breakdown.wave/report[4] around the real numbers; named the Ashen Pursuit wind-up as the step-back tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing from any source, including Soul Ignition's end-of-duration refund of the damage he took. Calling anti-heal optional talks the reader out of the item that beats his sustain.
audit.corrected: Replaced that clause with the Grievous Wounds line.

notes: No mirror exists yet for this pairing, so these findings are the ones the locke__ziggs side should reuse. Two data cautions, both left unwritten rather than asserted: the kit file tags Soul Ignition with trueDamage and Purgatory with grounding, but Riot's descriptions in the same file mention neither — per the trust-the-description rule I made no true-damage or grounding claim. That matters because the page repeatedly promises a held Satchel Charge bounces Ziggs clear of the Purgatory zone; if Purgatory does ground, that promise is false and appears in spikes[1], mid, whys[4] and wants.you[1]. See questionsForUser. Also unresolved: the page calls the Q 'Ritual Nails' while the kit description says 'Soul Nails' — I did not rename it.
